problem:
$$
r(y,\theta )=⟨\text{_______},\,y,\,\operatorname{csc}⁡y\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta ⟩
$$

The vector-valued function $r(y,\theta )$ above parametrizes the surface of revolution generated by rotating the curve $x=\operatorname{csc}⁡y$ by $2\pi $ radians about the $y$-axis for $y\in [\frac{\pi }{6},\frac{\pi }{2}].$ What is the first component of $r?$

feedback.problem:
$$
r(y,\theta )=⟨\text{_______},\,y,\,({y}^{3}-{y}^{4})\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta ⟩
$$

The vector-valued function $r(y,\theta )$ above parametrizes the surface of revolution generated by rotating the curve $x={y}^{3}-{y}^{4}$ by $2\pi $ radians about the $y$-axis for $y\in [0,1].$ What is the first component of $r?$
feedback.worked_solution:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14071875/assets/be6fb27c0d050a7007e9f4a0d526daaff40b8f7d01f20c63ac8cc00074121f28.png)

  

A point $(x,y,z)$ on the surface generated by rotating the graph of $x=f(y)$ by $2\pi $ radians about the $y$-axis has the position vector

$$
\begin{aligned}r=⟨f(y)\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta ,\,y,\,f(y)\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta ⟩,\,y\in [a,b],\,\theta =[0,2\pi ).\end{aligned}
$$

First, notice that $x=f(y)={y}^{3}-{y}^{4}\ge 0$ for all $y\in [0,1].$

So, the parametrization of our surface of revolution is

$$
r(y,\theta )=⟨({y}^{3}-{y}^{4})\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta ,\,y,\,({y}^{3}-{y}^{4})\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta ⟩,\,y\in [0,1],\,\theta \in [0,2\pi ).
$$

  

Therefore, the first component of $r$ is $({y}^{3}-{y}^{4})\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta .$
